title: Patient Financial Services Policy: Patient Payment Plans Enrollment Terms and Tier Selection
content:
This section of the Patient Financial Services policy sets the enrollment terms of the Patient Payment Plans: which tier is offered, what a proposal must carry, and who prepares it.

### 3.1 Total to be enrolled

The total to be enrolled on a plan is the sum of the amounts enrolled on it as initial enrollments or add-ons, from the proposal to the handling date.

### 3.2 Tier offered

The tier offered is one whose balance range contains the total to be enrolled, that is, a total between the tier's smallest enrolled balance and its largest balance, both figures inclusive. Where two tiers fit, the patient chooses.

### 3.3 Down payment (no longer in force)

The clause under which the down payment was the tier's down payment percentage of the total, rounded to the cent and not less than the tier's minimum down payment where the percentage is above 0.00, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the down payment at signing.

### 3.4 Installment (no longer in force)

The clause under which the installment was the total less the down payment divided by the tier's term, rounded to the cent, with the final installment absorbing any rounding difference, and was raised to the tier's minimum installment with the plan ending sooner, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for the installment written into the signed agreement.

### 3.5 Setup fee (no longer in force)

The clause under which the tier's setup fee, where above 0.00, is enrolled into the plan balance at signing and spread with the rest is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for setup fees and add-on fees.

### 3.6 Interest

The annual percentage rate is 0.00 on every tier, so no interest ever accrues on a plan.

### 3.7 Automatic debit and due day

Where the tier requires automatic debit, the proposal must carry an automatic debit method. The due day is any day from 1 to the tier's latest due day.

### 3.8 Who prepares the proposal

Where the tier requires counselor review, the proposal is prepared by a financial counselor within the tier's counselor review time in business days. Where the tier allows portal self-enrollment, the patient may also set the plan up in the MyLinden portal.

### 3.9 Hardship approval

The Financial Hardship Plan requires, on the patient's billing account, a hardship approval whose approved-through date is on or after the proposal date. A tier that requires hardship approval is offered only on that approval. The approval is judged on the system record of the billing account whose charges the plan covers, before the proposal is made.

| Approved-through date on the billing account, compared with the proposal date | Hardship approval current for the proposal |
|---|---|
| Later than the proposal date | Yes |
| The same day as the proposal date | Yes |
| Earlier than the proposal date | No |
| No approval recorded | No |

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- Where a hypothetical total to be enrolled equals the largest balance of one tier's range and also the smallest enrolled balance of another tier's range, both figures are inclusive, so both tiers fit and the patient chooses between them.
- A proposal dated 1 May for the Financial Hardship Plan against a billing account whose approval runs through 1 May meets 3.9; an approval that ran through 30 April does not.

superseded_clauses: The tier's setup_fee_usd, where above 0.00, is enrolled into the plan balance at signing and spread with the rest
The down payment is down_payment_pct of the total, rounded to the cent, but not less than down_payment_min_usd where down_payment_pct is above 0.00.

The installment is the total less the down payment divided by term_months, rounded to the cent, with the final installment absorbing any rounding difference; when that falls below min_installment_usd the installment is min_installment_usd and the plan simply ends sooner.
